bullets.title: GOOGL drops 4-5% on Hassabis leadership transition, Jeff Dean exit
bullets.body: Alphabet shares declined 4-5%, erasing ~$200B in market cap, after DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis stepped down to become Chairman (with Koray Kavukcuoglu taking over as head) and Chief AI Scientist Jeff Dean announced departure to start his own company. Google is simultaneously in talks for a $1.5B+ deal with AI coding startup Mechanize, and remains the 2nd-largest company globally behind NVDA after surpassing AAPL in market cap.

bullets.title: ANET posts seventh triple play in two years; analyst calls last night's call 'one of the best in years'
bullets.body: Arista Networks reported its seventh triple play in two years (third consecutive), with shares rallying 4.6%. One analyst who counts ANET as an early GAI infrastructure investment alongside NVDA said the earnings call was among the company's best, with key risks around customer concentration, top account loss, and white box displacement all appearing mitigated.

bullets.title: NVDA: $100M+ bearish options flow despite stock near 2-month highs; NVDA invests $2B each in COHR and LITE
bullets.body: NVDA hit a 2-month high (+4.3%) but saw nearly $100M in bearish options flow intraday, suggesting traders are positioning for a reversal. Separately, NVDA has secured multibillion-dollar purchase commitments and capacity rights from both Coherent and Lumentum with $2B investments in each, strategically positioning it ahead of downstream competitors.

bullets.title: FCC ban on Chinese optical transceivers bullish for COHR, LITE, AAOI
bullets.body: A proposed FCC restriction on Chinese data-center optical transceivers is being characterized as a material market redistribution event. LITE, COHR, and AAOI are positioned as primary domestic beneficiaries, while Chinese optical module stocks face a selloff. GlobalFoundries' Q2 call separately flagged AI optical-networking demand accelerating faster than available supply, reinforcing the structural demand picture.

bullets.title: UBER CEO flags strong consumer, bookings accelerating; stock seen as generational buy at Waymo parity
bullets.body: Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told CNBC 'the consumer is strong' and overall bookings accelerated in Q2 — the fourth straight quarter above 20% gross bookings growth. Multiple fintwit accounts note UBER now trades at the same valuation as Waymo and see the stock reaching $100 when fully autonomous rides are deployed without safety drivers in SF/Austin/LA, a milestone expected in Q4/Q1. Pershing Square holds UBER as third-largest position but is down 15% on the stake in 2024.

bullets.title: AAPL: BofA reiterates Buy, $380 PT; $400M+ call wall at $310
bullets.body: Bank of America maintained its Buy rating and $380 price target on Apple, citing a 28% surge in purchase commitments to $57B as a signal of iPhone production ramp and component stockpiling. Options desks note a large $400M+ call wall at $310.

bullets.title: AMD beats on datacenter revenue (+107% YoY) but AI forward guidance disappoints
bullets.body: AMD posted 107% year-over-year growth in datacenter revenue but failed to meet Wall Street's AI guidance expectations, following a pattern of AI hardware companies beating results but underwhelming on outlook. One analyst countered that the '$800M CapEx surprise' narrative is overblown and represents a sound investment.

bullets.title: PLTR: Army alone accounts for over a third of $5.1B in federal billings since 2010
bullets.body: Twitter analysis notes the U.S. Army has contributed $1.9B of Palantir's $5.1B in total federal contract obligations since 2010, representing over one-third of government revenue. Separately, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra outperformed frontier models on Palantir customer tasks without post-training.

bullets.title: MU crosses $1 trillion market cap; SNDK sees $2450 PT with analyst 'loading the truck'
bullets.body: Micron's market cap recovered above $1 trillion. One options-focused analyst highlighted active OTM December $30 call buying in NextNav ($NN) tied to spectrum utility speculation. Separately, an analyst issued a high-conviction reiteration of a $2,450 price target on SNDK, calling it 'superior risk/reward' and expressing willingness to be aggressively long at current levels.

bullets.title: MSFT: Nadella cites Morgan Stanley ROIC report showing 31% IaaS and 46% TaaS returns; Burry dumps MSFT bets
bullets.body: Satya Nadella highlighted a Morgan Stanley ROIC report showing 31% returns for hyperscaler IaaS and 46% for the TaaS (Token As a Service) layer as evidence of strong cloud economics. Separately, Michael Burry exited Microsoft positions while warning of a potential 1987-style market top.

bullets.title: NET Q2 preview: growth momentum intact, security emerging as core driver
bullets.body: Preview analysis on Cloudflare's Q2 2026 suggests Q2 channel performance remains strong with growth likely to accelerate from Q1. Base case for 2H26 is stable to modestly accelerating, with security emerging as the incremental growth driver.

bullets.title: AMZN: Only mega-cap at all-time highs; Zoox launches paid robotaxi in Las Vegas
bullets.body: AMZN is the only mega-cap trading at all-time highs per Bespoke. Amazon's Zoox division is beginning paid robotaxi service in Las Vegas, its first commercial deployment. One analyst flagged that Amazon's AI chip value estimates are inflated by internal software running on Graviton and Trainium, making the headline figures misleading for assessing actual third-party chip sales.

bullets.title: DIS CEO fires back at CMCSA on theme park strength; $24B content investment by FY26
bullets.body: Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro took a direct swipe at Universal parent Comcast after CMCSA flagged theme park sector weakness, stating Disney is 'performing significantly better than competition.' Disney also disclosed plans to invest $24B in content by FY26, with cruise future bookings appearing strong, offset by Q4 consumer weakness in Hong Kong and Shanghai.

bullets.title: AI equity funds down sharply in July; Citadel +6% via Situational Awareness liquidation; Whale Rock -21.7%
bullets.body: AI equity funds were down massively in July despite strong YTD gains. Citadel's flagship fund returned +5.9% in July (12% YTD) by acquiring Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness AI stock portfolio at a discount. Whale Rock's flagship fell 21.7% in July (-18.8% Long Only) but remains 35%+ ahead of benchmarks YTD. Coatue is only +14% YTD, which fintwit notes is underwhelming given its aggressive AI positioning.

bullets.title: Fed's Kashkari advocates gradual rate hikes targeting 2% inflation; September decision split 49/47
bullets.body: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said it is 'time to start slowly moving interest rates up,' targeting 2% inflation and not aiming to slow the economy—though he clarified he is 'not calling for a dramatic increase.' Prediction markets show a 49% hold / 47% +25bp split for September, with BofA forecasting three hikes (Sep/Oct/Dec) vs. JPM, Goldman, and Morgan Stanley expecting holds.

bullets.title: BofA: S&P 500 hit 2026 target at 7,741; technical upside to 8,541 with 7,500 support
bullets.body: Bank of America's technical team says the S&P 500 has reached its 2026 price target of 7,741, with the technical setup suggesting a rally toward 8,000, 8,234, and 8,541. Key support is at 7,500 with August-October flagged as a seasonally weak warning period. The Dow closed above 54k for the first time ever; Nasdaq has rallied 1%+ for four consecutive days (only 18th time in history).

bullets.title: Michael Burry warns of 1987-style major market top
bullets.body: Michael Burry publicly warned that the market is 'near the top,' citing 1987-style crash risk, while also acknowledging that S&P 500 record highs could attract fresh money that extends the rally. Burry also dumped his Microsoft bets as part of the move. BTIG separately noted 'echoes from DotCom' and urged investors 'don't get burned twice.'

bullets.title: ADP payrolls miss sharply at 44K vs. 65K consensus; ISM Services 54.1 misses but prices paid surge
bullets.body: ADP private employment rose just 44K in July versus 65K consensus and 95-98K prior, with healthcare driving nearly all gains and goods-producing industries posting net losses. ISM Services came in at 54.1 (vs. 54.5 expected), but prices paid spiked to 70.3 vs. 65.0 consensus while employment dropped to 47.4 vs. 51.2 expected—stagflationary mix within services. Goldman maintained its 75K official payroll forecast citing weak ADP-NFP correlation.

bullets.title: Copper hits $14,000 ($6.68/lb); gold +3-4%; silver +5%—macro commodity surge
bullets.body: Copper topped $14,000 as US stockpiling drains global supply ahead of potential Trump tariffs. Spot gold extended gains to $4,238/oz (+4%), silver rose to $62.53/oz (+5%), and precious metals miners like AEM surged 9% on the session. The macro commodity move is being driven by a combination of Hormuz deal optimism, Iran sanctions removal, and safe-haven demand.

bullets.title: GLW: Q2 Solar sales +90% YoY to $438M despite $7M loss; Section 232 tariff beneficiary thesis
bullets.body: Corning is identified as the most direct U.S.-listed fundamental beneficiary of a potential U.S. polysilicon price floor and Section 232 tariff regime. Q2 2026 Solar sales reached $438M, up 90% from $231M in the prior year, though the segment posted a $7M net loss. The policy framing is characterized as a supply chain restructuring event rather than a conventional tariff.
